title: Inside the model: 24 blocks
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Sizes from brain3d/trace.json model_card; vectors from films/structure_data.json.

blocks.text: This is the inside of the model: a stack of 24 blocks, one on top of another, all built the same way.
blocks.say: This is the inside of the model: a stack of twenty-four blocks, one on top of another, all built the same way.

blocks.text: Each block has two parts. The first is attention, made of 14 heads working side by side. Each head lets a token look back at the tokens before it.
blocks.say: Each block has two parts. The first is attention, made of fourteen heads working side by side. Each head lets a token look back at the tokens before it.

blocks.text: The second part is the feed-forward network, 4,864 numbers wide. It works on each token's vector by itself, without looking at the others.
blocks.say: The second part is the feed-forward network, four thousand eight hundred and sixty-four numbers wide. It works on each token's vector by itself, without looking at the others.

blocks.text: Now send in Emma's question. All 100 tokens enter at the bottom, each one a vector of 896 numbers. In every block, attention lets each token gather from the ones before it, then the feed-forward part reworks each vector on its own. All 100 vectors come out changed, and climb to the next block.
blocks.say: Now send in Emma's question. All one hundred tokens enter at the bottom, each one a vector of eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. In every block, attention lets each token gather from the ones before it, then the feed-forward part reworks each vector on its own. All one hundred vectors come out changed, and climb to the next block.

blocks.text: After 24 blocks, the vectors reach the top. Next, we open attention, and see what the heads look at.
blocks.say: After twenty-four blocks, the vectors reach the top. Next, we open attention, and see what the heads look at.
